ASTRA ASSEMBLY INVESTIGATION — SECOND-STAGE CONSTRUCTION
2026-11-01

DECISION

The consequential opening survives, but the preferred mechanism has changed.
Temporary guides are no longer the main route. I constructed a completion-
dependent physical recovery operation, exposed and removed an avoidable
recycling bypass, then allowed a stronger conventional recovery process to
take over most of that service. Its possible integration advantage is too
narrow and unmeasured to carry the ambition.

The principal target is now manufacture of a continuous, chemically specified
23S RNA without taking that RNA from an existing ribosome, followed by
repeatable full translation. The independent covalent construction supplied
an exact material route. I reconciled it with the functional recovery work,
complete cost accounting and a matched preparation experiment that separates
chemical specification, material damage and inherited folding history.

There is no new wet-lab result, demonstrated resource advantage, closed
factory or proven general assembly principle here. The return consists of
specific molecular constructions, actual structural/chemical source analysis,
ordinary proofs, executable evidence, and failures that changed the choice.

WHY THIS CAPABILITY MATTERS

A manufactured ribosome is a potentially general machine for making other
protein machines. Existing purified-component constructions still leave
important dependencies on native RNA, undefined extracts, supplied factors,
modified precursors or living-system production. Removing the native-RNA
dependence would enable deliberate chemical construction of the machine's
central scaffold, including chemical states that a DNA sequence alone does
not specify. That is a substantial molecular-manufacturing capability even
before autonomous reproduction is possible.

The target is a material object with known chemical composition and measured
working service. Recovering its rRNA genotype through reverse transcription
and PCR is a different service; those operations do not reproduce its full
modification pattern or assembled state. Normal recycling can re-pair
subunits, so the retained identity is a23S/50S lineage, not a permanent70S pair.

USEFUL FAILURES AND PRECISE RETAINED BOUNDARIES
2026-11-01. Companion to CONSTRUCTION.txt and the first-stage archive.

H98 RELEASE BY MATURE-CONTACT REASONING
Rejected as an earned mechanism. The trapped9DYG state acquires a protein
anchor absent from the mature-contact simplification. Its missing sidechains
and missingC2498 domain do not provide energies or accessibility. H98/uL13
can also participate productively in the source's proposed assembly route.
Prehybridization rescue does not establish postbinding release in a protein-
containing intermediate. ASO sequences remain unavailable from the blocked
supplement; no invented sequence is present in the construction.

H98 TAGGING AS A HARMLESS HANDLE
The2023 H98-MS2 study, DOI10.1261/rna.079690.123, shows that ordinary function
can coexist with impaired resistance to a60C challenge. An addedA that
restores the native quartet changes the thermal phenotype. This is evidence
to measure lifetime after engineering; it is not a numerical lifetime model
at normal translation temperatures. Geometry and transient activity alone
do not make a modification neutral.

PHOTOLYTIC RNA BANDAGES
Richards2008, DOI10.1016/j.bmcl.2008.09.093, demonstrates one two-arm2'OMe
construction with inhibited expression and substantial restoration after
photolysis. Other strongly binding versions fail to restore expression.
This earns a real cleavage/release lead but not vacating a ribosomal
protein-containing intermediate, or a reusable guide without chemical
replacement. UV burden, residual arms, damage and release kinetics matter.

RSMB AS A NOVEL UNIVERSAL HANDOFF
Not claimed. Wei/Woodson2026, DOI10.1126/sciadv.aef7741, already supplies
specific16S3'-domain remodeling, changedS7/S19 interactions and catalysis-
associated release. The exact isolated-domain experiment is narrower than
active30S manufacture. StableS7 capture requires prompt cooperative protein
access; simply removingRsmB and waiting is not equivalent. The static
affinity calculation uses mutant/substrate/product mimics and cannot be
substituted for WT driven kinetics. See RSMB_OPERATION.json and the
strongest-native-construction record.

S7 SURFACE CAPTURE
Duss2019, DOI10.1016/j.cell.2019.10.035, earns native cooperativeS7 capture
and useful activity of the reported labeling construct. It does not earn an
arbitrary surface attachment, surface-compatible reconstitution

# Deposited-coordinate geometry audit
The table gives minimum modeled heavy-atom distances in angstroms. Protein comparisons use only matched backbone atoms (N/CA/C/O), because 9DYG lacks uL13 sidechains. It does not estimate an interaction strength or rate.

| Residue pair / selection | Mature 4YBB | RA20-B-c 9DYG |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| RNA 9-2800 | 2.700 | 32.183 |
| RNA 10-2629 | 3.019 | 37.840 |
| RNA 9-2629 | 2.795 | 42.406 |
| RNA 10-2800 | 3.071 | 27.525 |
| RNA 2797 to uL13 backbone | 18.425 | 6.300 |
| RNA 2798 to uL13 backbone | 15.919 | 7.736 |
| RNA 2799 to uL13 backbone | 12.897 | 6.560 |
| RNA 2800 to uL13 backbone | 10.719 | 5.751 |

The native quartet is geometrically absent in the inhibited model, while part of the H98 apical neighborhood approaches uL13. This supports the published interaction-exchange interpretation. It does not establish that the nonnative anchor is harmful, or that suppressing it would improve assembly.
